reachable:
Yes on both counts, checked by execution rather than by reading.

REACHES THE SCORED PREDICTION. I built the real scored layout — cups_probe._load_standardized_seqs(dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd, "inner") -> harvest_cups_windows -> build_cups_layout, filtered to the scored slice (N in 3,4,5 and depth >= 3), 64 windows, L = 47 — ran the candidate, took pred[arange, rpos] (exactly what cups_probe._fwd_pred scores), then perturbed ONLY tp_read.weight (N(0, 0.02)) and re-ran. Result: max |dpred| at the scored read position = 0.190, and 64/64 rows changed. So the transport channel is not merely present, it moves the exact vector the N-way forced-foil argmin consumes. rpos is even on every row (min 22, max 46), which is required because the contribution is only added at pred[:, 0::2] (arch__r23_pointer_transport_memory.py:179).

CORRECT GATING AT THE READ. At the scored read step valid_cmd is True on all 64 rows and valid_obs is False on all 64 (the target obs is withheld), so wr = 0 there via `wr * (valid_cmd & valid_obs)` and `_pad_steps` (arch__r23_pointer_transport_memory.py:94-96). The read s is taken before the move/write inside the same step (:109-127), so the scored read sees the memory the earlier chain built and nothing the read step itself writes. This is consistent with the SCORING ground truth (cmd valid, obs invalid at exactly the final read).

GRADIENT IN TRAINING. Non-zero from backward #2 onward on all 13 tp_* tensors (see divergence 1 for the step-by-step trace). The training-side ground truth (collate clears cmd+obs together) does NOT disable this mechanism: nothing here is gated on "command present, observation absent". The write gate is gated on valid_obs, which in training is False only for steps the parent's occlusion dropped — which is the interaction the hypothesis claims, and it is real (occlusion runs first, at :144, before x_cmd/obs_tok/valid are derived from the occluded tensors).

THE ALGEBRA IS EXACT, NOT APPROXIMATE. I drove the real `_transport_reads` with injected orthogonal one-hot addresses (patching tp_src_sel/tp_dst_sel/tp_addr/_quotient/tp_move_gate/tp_write_gate as callables, leaving the loop body untouched) on the chain: write v0 at e0, write v1 at e1, mv e0->e2, mv e2->e3, mv e1->e4, read e3. Result: relerr(read@e3, v0) = 0.0 exactly (relerr to v1 = 1.42), read@e2 after one hop = v0 exactly, read@e1 = v1 exactly, occupancy 1.0 at the transported address and 0.0 at an unwritten one. The fused rank-2 bmm (:121-127) is algebraically identical to the stated read -> move -> write sequence, as claimed.

STRENGTH CAVEATS THE GATE DOES NOT COVER. (a) The author's stated load-bearing unverified assumption — that a linear readout of the pooled command embedding can separate first path from second path — actually HOLDS at the 768-d level, which I could check because the embeddings are outside the jail: ridge regression from the pooled "mv A B" embedding, held out 20%, retrieves "cat SRC" at 98.9% top-1 and "cat DST" at 97.4% top-1 against a 2541-path pool (chance 0.04%), and ranks DST above SRC 99.8% of the time. This is an upper bound, since the module's addresses must pass the shared 176-d cmd_proj bottleneck. (b) The author's failure mode 2 (address crosstalk) is live at initialization: on real cups streams, cross-command source-address cosine is mean 0.827 / p95 0.994 / max 0.999, i.e. the K=64 memory starts as very nearly one shared slot. Within a single command a·b = -0.25 mean (range -0.48..0.03), so the move operator itself is non-degenerate at init. Whether training decorrelates the addresses is not something I could determine without training; I did not run a full training job.
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says. Every load-bearing computational claim reproduced under execution: the two-address transport is exact (depth-2 chained move returns the source content with relative error 0.0, occupancy 1.0/0.0 as described); the fused rank-2 update is algebraically identical to the stated read -> move -> write ordering, with the read taken before the same step's write; the module is bit-for-bit identical to its r22 parent at initialization (max |dpred| = 0.0 and max |dh| = 0.0 in both eval and train mode with matched RNG state); the contribution is RMS-capped, zero-init, gated on [h_cmd, occupancy, read_rms], and added at command positions only; gates are zeroed on padded steps and the write gate is additionally gated on valid_obs, which is the claimed occlusion interaction; the optim co-design is real (executed: tp_addr.weight routes into the Muon addressing group alongside file_read/file_write/path_read/path_write/tr_path, and tp_read.weight sits under the spectral cap with tr_read.weight); the head still sees transition_from_emb with _disabled = False returning [N,768]; parameter count is 665,045 new on 3,739,739 total, matching the stated 665k on 3.74M; shapes and finiteness hold for L in {0,1,2,3,9,40,47}, an all-padded batch predicts exactly 0, x50 inputs stay finite, and causality holds (max |dpred| = 0.0 strictly before a perturbed position, 1.23 after). Only the arch axis differs from the parent genome, as claimed. The divergences are all in the prose around the mechanism, not the mechanism: one check in the "CHECKS I RAN" list is false as stated (gradients reach only 2 of 13 new tensors on the first backward, all 13 from the second), the description of where the addresses come from omits the learned 176-d projection and the trainable positional term (measured contamination small at init, but it is a route for chain position to enter the address, which is the one confound comp_ca does not structurally cancel), the budget ratio is loose (their own numbers give 1.79x, mine 1.46x, prose says 1.6x), the "crossover" imports no partner axis, and the quoted mv render string is one of two constants on this root. Separately worth recording for the archive: the single risk the author flagged as unverifiable from inside the jail is verifiable from outside and comes out favorable (98.9% / 97.4% held-out src / dst path retrieval from the pooled mv embedding over a 2541-path pool), while the crosstalk risk he also flagged is quantitatively live at init (cross-command address cosine mean 0.83, p95 0.99).

divergences.claim: "gradients are non-zero on every new tp_* parameter after one backward" (hypothesis.txt:149)
divergences.what_the_code_does: At initialization tp_read.weight and tp_read.bias are exactly zero (arch__r23_pointer_transport_memory.py:47-48), so contrib = g * tp_read(r*scale) has zero derivative with respect to BOTH r and g. On the first backward only 2 of the 13 tp_* tensors receive gradient (tp_read.weight, tp_read.bias). Every other tp_* parameter — tp_src_sel, tp_dst_sel, tp_addr, tp_move_gate, tp_write_gate, tp_out_gate — receives exactly zero gradient until tp_read.weight has moved off zero, which happens after optimizer step 1. This is a bootstrap ordering, not a dead mechanism: from backward #2 onward all 13 receive gradient.

divergences.claim: "Both are linear read-outs of frozen mean-pooled encoder vectors of whole command strings." (hypothesis.txt:120, describing a_i and b_i)
divergences.what_the_code_does: The addresses are read out of `x_cmd = self._cmd_features(...)` = LayerNorm(cmd_proj(z) + type_emb(0) + pos_scale * PE), i.e. a LEARNED 176-d projection of the frozen 768-d pooled vector with a trainable-scaled sinusoidal POSITIONAL term added, then layer-normed. So (a) the address passes through the shared 176-d trunk bottleneck rather than being a readout of the 768-d pooled vector, and (b) the address for the same command string is position-dependent. Measured at init the position contamination is small — the same real command embedding placed at 24 different command slots of a length-47 stream yields source addresses with pairwise cosine >= 0.9913 — but pos_scale is a trainable parameter, so this is a route by which chain position can enter the address, and chain position is precisely the confound comp_ca does NOT cancel structurally.

divergences.claim: "This is where the crossover with the plain-transformer partner is real rather than cosmetic." (hypothesis.txt:89-90)
divergences.what_the_code_does: genome.json adopts NO axis from the partner. The partner genome is all-baseline (objective mse, arch baseline_transformer, optim baseline_adamw, target identity, batcher baseline_uniform, stream baseline_interleave, head baseline_passthrough); the candidate keeps the parent's objective / optim / batcher / head verbatim and changes only arch. The "crossover" is realized purely as an argument that a gate which can close leaves the trunk prediction standing. The hypothesis is honest about this on its face ("preserved as the fallback branch"), so it is not a false statement about the code — but the archive record should not read as if a partner mechanism was imported.
